anomaly.summary: This anomaly occurs when a compute which writes to a data register is issued in parallel with a move from the same data register to a DAG register (Type 5a instruction). If a use of the DAG register occurs within 6 cycles of the move, and an unrelated stall occurs during the intervening cycles, then the DAG register use may receive the wrong value.
anomaly.compiler-behavior: The compiler ensures that the same register is never used for both the target data register of the compute and the source register of the move to DAG register when a Type 5a instruction is used.
anomaly.assembler-behavior: The assembler issues a diagnostic for instruction sequences that may be subject to the anomaly.

anomaly.summary: BTB Software return prediction uses the value held in register i12 to speculatively start fetching instructions at the return address of a function. If i12 doesn't contain a valid address, these speculative fetches can cause the hardware to malfunction. This BTB feature should only be enabled if the application code can guarantee that i12 always holds valid return addresses. From ADSP-SC58x silicon revision 1.0 the boot code disables BTB, addressing the related 20000005 silicon anomaly.
anomaly.rtl-behavior: The compiler and runtime library may use the i12 register for values that are not valid code addresses. Therefore the CRT startup code ensures that software return optimization is disabled when it enables the BTB.

anomaly.summary: Range-based invalidation and write back invalidation of the L1 cache using the FLUSH instruction has the following restrictions: (1) Interrupts must be disabled during the flush operation. To avoid long interrupt latencies, the entire range should be split into smaller ranges. (2) The FLUSH instruction should be padded with 5 unrelated instructions.
anomaly.compiler-behavior: The FLUSH instruction is not generated by the compiler.
anomaly.rtl-behavior: The FLUSH instruction is used only by the function 'flush_data_buffer()'. This function flushes each cache line individually and executes 5 NOPs after the FLUSH instruction when built for parts that require the workaround.

anomaly.summary: If an IDLE instruction occurs within 5 cycles of a cacheable memory access, incorrect behavior may occur when L1 cache is enabled.
anomaly.compiler-behavior: The compiler ensures that an IDLE instruction is separated by at least five cycles from a preceding memory access. It also ensures that no memory access occurs in the last five cycles of an interrupt handler, so that an interrupt may safely return to an IDLE instruction.
anomaly.assembler-behavior: The assembler issues diagnostic ea2561 when an IDLE instruction may follow a memory access within 5 cycles. It also issues diagnostic ea2562 when a memory access is used in the last five cycles of an interrupt handler which returns via the RTI instruction. This may fail if the interrupt returns directly to an IDLE instruction.

anomaly.summary: When SIMD mode is enabled, a value loaded into ASTATy from memory or a register cannot be used in a condition within 5 cycles.
anomaly.assembler-behavior: The assembler issues warning ea2566 for instruction sequences that may be subject to the anomaly.
anomaly.rtl-defs: WA_20000016 (in order for this macro to be defined, the user must include the header file <sys/anomaly_macros_rtl.h>)

anomaly.summary: Speculative read accesses launched on pipeline flush may lead to system hang under some conditions.
anomaly.loader-behavior: The preload and init code executables provided in CCES for the ADSP-SC584 and ADSP-SC589 EZ-Kit support have changes to disable speculative accesses to unused DMC and SMC memory using the SMPU as required to work around this anomaly. The source for the preloads and init code also has a workaround for SPI flash memory, but it is disabled in the executables provided in CCES. If you do not use SPI flash memory at all, either in your application or in the boot process, you can rebuild the preload or init code with the UNUSED_SPI_FLASH #define set to 1. Alternatively, if SPI flash is used only in certain parts of your application, use the workaround during execution of parts of your program where SPI memory is not set up and therefore speculative accesses must not be performed. The workaround consists of executing the following three lines of code (be sure to include the <sys/platform.h> header to provide the necessary macros): *pREG_SPI2_TXCTL = (BITM_SPI_TXCTL_TEN | BITM_SPI_TXCTL_TTI); *pREG_SPI2_RXCTL = (BITM_SPI_RXCTL_REN | BITM_SPI_RXCTL_RTI); *pREG_SPI2_CTL = (BITM_SPI_CTL_EN|BITM_SPI_CTL_MSTR| BITM_SPI_CTL_MMSE); This workaround to avoid speculative accesses to SPI flash is not required on silicon revisions 1.0 and later.

anomaly.summary: Address hole in DDR VISA space
anomaly.compiler-behavior: The LDFs work around this anomaly by not mapping VISA code to the unmapped address range.

anomaly.summary: When L1 cache is enabled, a byte load or store using the PM data bus should not immediately follow any load or store to external memory using the DM data bus.
anomaly.compiler-behavior: The compiler ensures that two loads or stores that can together cause the anomaly are always separated by at least one instruction.
anomaly.assembler-behavior: The assembler issues a diagnostic for instruction sequences that may be subject to the anomaly.

anomaly.summary: When performing an exclusive load or store, the ASTAT register is not updated until five cycles later. Therefore to make sure that the correct register value is used, an exclusive load or store should be separated by at least five cycles from a subsequent read or write of the ASTAT register.
anomaly.compiler-behavior: The compiler ensures that an exclusive load or store is always separated by at least five cycles from a subsequent read or write of the condition code register.
anomaly.assembler-behavior: The assembler issues warning ea2563 for instruction sequences that may be subject to the anomaly.

anomaly.summary: The address used in a SIMD short-word (SW-qualified) memory access should be aligned on a two-byte boundary.
anomaly.compiler-behavior: The compiler does not use SIMD mode for any SW-qualified memory access whose address may not be aligned on a two-byte boundary.

anomaly.summary: Read data corruption may occur if three or more writes to external memory and three or more reads from external memory occur within a window of four instructions.
anomaly.compiler-behavior: The compiler ensures that four consecutive instructions never perform both three or more loads and three or more stores when these accesses may be to external memory.
anomaly.assembler-behavior: The assembler issues warning ea2558 for instruction sequences that may be subject to the anomaly.
anomaly.rtl-behavior: The runtime libraries include workarounds for this anomaly in functions memcpy, transpm, vecsadd, vecsmlt, rfftn, ifftn and cfftn. The libraries are built with assembler detection for anomaly 20000024 enabled and confirmed to not trigger the warning. Note that the cfftf, ifftf and rfftf functions sources suppress the assembler warning for 20000024 as these functions are documented to only work with internal memory buffers so cannot trigger the 20000024 anomaly.

anomaly.summary: For DM and PM Cache, last line of WAY1 is not written-back when the Full Cache Write-Back functionality is used by setting the Write-back bits of the Cache Configuration register.
anomaly.rtl-behavior: There are workarounds for anomaly 20000028 in the dcache_invalidate() and dcache_invalidate_both() functions.

anomaly.summary: L1 Cache performance degrades under certain conditions.
anomaly.rtl-behavior: Worked around by not having an uncached range for MCAPI for the L1 MP addresses to avoid external memory code execution being uncached. MCAPI copies L1 data to intermediate buffers in uncached L2 memory instead.

anomaly.summary: Read data corruption may occur if a conditional memory write instruction is immediately followed by a type 3c memory read instruction.
anomaly.assembler-behavior: The assembler works around the anomaly by expanding affected 16-bit type 3c instructions to 48-bit type 3a instructions.

anomaly.summary: If TIMER is configured in External Clock mode with a period of n, the first interrupt or trigger will occur after n+1 clocks while subsequent interrupts/triggers will occur every n clocks.
anomaly.ssldd-behavior: The timer service works around the anomaly by decreasing the timer period by one for the first timer interrupt only.

anomaly.summary: System MMRs accesses fail if accessed from L2/L3 when SHARC+ instruction cache is enabled.
anomaly.rtl-behavior: Worked around by keeping the instruction cache disabled, including when the application explicitly enables cache. Data caches are also kept disabled, as a consequence of this.

anomaly.summary: EMDMA transfers may fail if the DMA address range crosses the boundary of a 4KByte block of SHARC L1 memory, when the address modifier is set to 1.
anomaly.ssldd-behavior: There is no support for EMDMA transfer provided currently. Future support is planned and will include the required workaround.

anomaly.summary: DMC read state machine may not be in correct state after DMC initialization.
anomaly.rtl-behavior: The preload/initcodes provided will perform the required workaround before applications are loaded

anomaly.summary: TMU Fault and Alert Status Bits Cannot Be Individually Cleared
anomaly.ssldd-behavior: The anomaly workaround is used in the CCES TMU driver.

anomaly.summary: Single writes to the SPI_SLVSEL register do not take effect.
This anomaly occurs when an instruction that targets the PCSTK register is immediately followed by an access to L2 or L3 memory. In this case the write to the PCSTK register may have no effect.
anomaly.compiler-behavior: The compiler ensures that a write to the PCSTK register is not immediately followed by a memory access.
anomaly.rtl-behavior: There are workarounds for anomaly 20000069 in the interrupt dispatcher functions.

anomaly.summary: The SPI Slave Transmit DMA Peripheral Interrupt may be generated before all data has been transferred to the master device.
Interrupts may not latch when aligned with an explicit SHARC+ core write to the IRPTL register. There are workarounds for this anomaly in the uC/OS-II and uC/OS-III products.

A pre-modify memory load or store can malfunction if one of the DAG registers involved in computing the address is written by a universal register move within the previous four instructions, and in turn the source register of the move is written by a compute or data register load during the four instructions prior to that. The issue occurs when a pipeline flush occurs during the sequence.
anomaly.compiler-behavior: The compiler inserts NOP instructions where necessary to avoid the anomaly.
anomaly.assembler-behavior: The assembler issues warning ea2569 for instruction sequences that may be subject to the anomaly.

anomaly.summary: Reads of a DDR controller's DMC_CPHY_CTL register return incorrect values. A read or write of the register raises a false data read or write error interrupt.

A type 18 bit operation on a USTAT register can malfunction if the preceding three instructions are memory accesses involving the same USTAT register, whereby the first two instructions have to be a load and a store targeting external memory or system MMR space, and the third instruction has to be a load from core MMR space.
anomaly.assembler-behavior: The assembler issues warning ea2571 for instruction sequences that may be subject to the anomaly.

anomaly.summary: When cache memory is disabled, core accesses to L2/L3 memory space may return stale data from the data prefetch buffer if there is a pending write to the same L2/L3 address space.
anomaly.rtl-behavior: The anomaly is worked around by disabling the data prefetch buffer in the startup code when either of the DM and PM data caches is disabled.

anomaly.summary: The standard DMC PHY calibration procedure may not work as expected, resulting in incorrect driver impedance and ODT calibration. This may cause DDR access failures.
anomaly.rtl-behavior: The preload/initcodes provided perform the DMC PHY initialization using an alternative method that ensures correct calibration.
